title: How to block a sender in Gmail on Mac: step by step for the browser
metaTitle: How to Block a Sender in Gmail on Mac (Browser Steps)
description: How to block a sender in Gmail on Mac: open their email, click More next to Reply, choose Block. Also covers unblocking and Apple Mail.
targetKeyword: how to block a sender in gmail on mac
intro: To block a sender in Gmail on Mac, open one of their emails in your browser, click More next to Reply, and choose Block. Gmail then sends future mail from that address to Spam, but messages already in your inbox stay where they are.
tldr: Gmail on Mac runs in your browser. Open a message from the sender, click More next to Reply, then choose Block.
Future mail from that address goes to Spam. Mail already in your inbox does not move on its own.
To undo the block, use the same More menu, or go to Settings > See all settings > Filters and blocked addresses.
Apple Mail on Mac has its own Block Contact option, and it can hold up to 3,000 senders.
Google's keyboard shortcut list has no shortcut for blocking. Its other shortcuts work only after you turn them on in Settings.

blocks.text: Gmail on Mac runs in a browser

The Gmail help pages this guide relies on describe Gmail in a web browser. They do not mention a separate Gmail app for Mac. So the steps here run in Safari, Chrome or Firefox at mail.google.com. Google's blocking help page covers the desktop version without naming a Mac or a macOS version.

This matters for one reason. Google can move menu items when it changes the layout. If a label looks different on your screen, look for the same words. Block, Unblock and More are the labels to watch.
Block a sender in Gmail on Mac, step by step

The numbered steps at the top of this guide follow the open-message route, which is the one Google documents. Before you click Block, read the item carefully. It should show the sender's name or address. If it shows a name you do not recognise, close the menu and check the sender line again.
Three places to block a sender on a Mac

You can block from an open message, from the inbox list, or from the Apple Mail app. Google's help page covers the open-message route. Security.org's 2026 Gmail guide describes the inbox-list route, with a checkbox, the three dots above the list, and Block. That guide also says it has no macOS-specific steps, so treat it as a secondary source.

rows: More (three dots) next to Reply > Block [sender's name]
Tick the message > More (three dots) above the list > Block [sender's name]
Hover over the sender's name > click the arrow > Block Contact
Blocked mail stays in Inbox with a mark, or moves to Trash, based on your setting
blocks.caption: Three routes to block a sender on a Mac, and what each one does next.

blocks.text: What blocking does and does not do

Blocking changes where new mail from one address lands. It does not reach back into your inbox. Gmail's help says future emails from a blocked sender go to Spam. Anything that arrived before the block stays where it is until you move it or delete it.

items: Future mail from that exact address goes to Spam.
Older messages from the sender stay in whichever folder they are in.
Gmail keeps flagging the sender as spam, even after you clear their messages from Spam.
Blocking works per address. A second address from the same company still gets through.
Unblocking sends future mail from that address back to your inbox.

blocks.title: Blocking is not a shield
blocks.text: A block stops one address. It does not stop a scam sent from a new address. If a message asks for a password, a payment or a code, report it as spam and do not reply or click links.
Unblock a sender in Gmail on Mac

The fastest way back is from a message from them. Open the message, click More next to Reply, and choose Unblock followed by the sender's name. If you cannot find a message from them, use the settings page instead. Settings > See all settings > Filters and blocked addresses lists the blocked addresses.

items: Click the Settings gear at the top right, then choose See all settings.
Open the Filters and blocked addresses tab.
Tick the box beside the sender's address.
Click Unblock selected addresses.

blocks.text: Block a whole company or domain

Gmail's block works one address at a time. A company that sends from several addresses needs one block for each. Several sources say a filter can catch a whole domain. Google's blocking page does not cover domains, and the filter steps are not on the pages this guide checked, so check Google's filter help before you rely on one. The guide to creating a filter on Mac has the menu paths: [how to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).
Block a sender in Apple Mail on Mac

If you read Gmail in the Mail app, blocking works differently. Apple's Sequoia guide describes the steps in the list below. Apple uses Block Contact in that guide and Block Sender in its junk-mail guide, so the menu may show either label.

items: Open a message from the sender in Mail.
Hover over the sender's name in the message header.
Click the arrow that appears.
Choose Block Contact. A Blocked icon appears by the sender's name.

blocks.text: Check the Blocked list in Mail

Go to Mail > Preferences in Sequoia, or Mail > Settings in the macOS 27 guide. Then choose Junk Mail > Blocked. Tick Enable blocked mail filtering. Next, pick what happens to blocked mail: leave it in your Inbox with a mark, or move it to the Trash. Apple says you can block up to 3,000 senders.
Some secondary sources say blocked mail is ignored unless that box is ticked. I did not confirm that on an Apple page. Keep the box ticked, then watch what happens to the sender's next message.
Keyboard shortcuts: what they can and cannot do
Google's shortcut list has no shortcut for blocking a sender. You need the menu for that. The shortcuts below speed up the rest of your inbox cleanup, and they stay off until you turn them on.

items: Turn them on: Settings gear > See all settings > Settings tab > Keyboard shortcuts > Keyboard shortcuts on > Save Changes.
r replies to the open message.
m mutes the conversation.
Shift and 1 reports the message as spam on a US keyboard.
. opens the more actions menu. Block is not a named shortcut, so you still click it.

blocks.text: Common mistakes when blocking a sender

items: Blocking the display name instead of the address. Two senders can share a name.
Expecting old mail to disappear. Blocking does not move existing messages.
Emptying Spam to undo the block. Gmail still flags the sender's mail as spam.
Assuming one block covers a new address. Each address needs its own block.
Setting the block in one app and checking another. Gmail web and Apple Mail use separate menus, so check the app you read mail in.

blocks.text: Still getting mail from a blocked sender?

Start in Spam. New mail from a blocked address should land there, so check it before you assume the block failed. If mail still arrives in your inbox, look for a filter that labels or forwards it, or for a second address the sender used. Apple Mail users should check the Blocked list and the setting for blocked mail.
A worked example with a repeat sender

Say a sender writes from billing@example.com every week, asking you to pay an invoice you do not recognise. You open the latest message, click More next to Reply, and choose Block. The next week a message arrives, and it lands in Spam. You open it, read the sender line, and report it as spam.

Then the same scam comes from billing@example.net. The block on the first address does nothing for that one. That is the moment to block the second address too, and to check whether a filter would fit better. The pattern matters more than either address.
How long Gmail keeps spam and trash

Google says emails in Trash or Spam are permanently deleted after 30 days. You can empty those folders sooner. If a blocked sender writes something you need, move it out of Spam within that window. Google's help does not describe a way to recover messages after they are gone.
Use Gmail in its own window with Chrome

Chrome can install a website as an app. That gives Gmail its own window, which helps if you check mail all day. On some sites an Install icon appears at the right of the address bar, and you can use that instead of the menu.

items: Open Gmail at mail.google.com in Google Chrome.
Click the three dots at the top right of Chrome, then choose Cast, save, and share.
Choose Install page as app.

blocks.text: The Gmail window still runs Gmail in Chrome, so every step in this guide still applies.
Where to go next

If you want to sort mail before it reaches your inbox, read [how to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail). If you sent a message to the wrong person, [how to undo send in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/undo-send-in-gmail) covers the browser and Apple Mail steps.

faq.question: Does blocking a sender in Gmail delete their old emails?
faq.answer: No. Gmail's help says future mail from a blocked sender goes to Spam. Older messages stay where they are until you move or delete them yourself.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: The Gmail help pages this guide uses describe Gmail in a web browser and do not mention a Mac app. Use mail.google.com in Safari, Chrome or Firefox. Chrome can also install Gmail as an app in its own window.

faq.question: How do I unblock someone in Gmail on Mac?
faq.answer: Open a message from them, click More next to Reply, and choose Unblock followed by their name. You can also go to Settings > See all settings > Filters and blocked addresses, tick the address, and click Unblock selected addresses.

faq.question: Does blocking stop a sender from reaching me?
faq.answer: Not exactly. Gmail still receives their mail, but it sends it to Spam. Their messages stay out of your inbox until you unblock them.

faq.question: Can I block a whole domain in Gmail on Mac?
faq.answer: Gmail's blocking page covers single addresses only. A filter may catch a whole domain, but check Google's filter steps before you rely on one. The filter guide on this site lists the menu paths.

faq.question: How do I block a sender in Apple Mail on Mac?
faq.answer: Hover over the sender's name in a message header, click the arrow, then choose Block Contact. Apple says you can block up to 3,000 senders in total.

faq.question: What happens to Spam and Trash after a while?
faq.answer: Google says emails in Trash or Spam are permanently deleted after 30 days. They can go sooner if you empty those folders yourself, so move anything you need out early.

task: Block a sender in Gmail on Mac
appliesTo: Gmail in Safari, Chrome or Firefox on macOS, and Apple Mail with a Gmail account
requirements: A Mac with Safari, Chrome or Firefox
A Gmail account you can sign in to
The sender's email address, or one of their messages

steps.name: Open Gmail in your browser
steps.text: Go to mail.google.com in Safari, Chrome or Firefox, then sign in to the account that receives the mail. Gmail's help pages describe the web version, so the steps below use it.
steps.tip: Sign in to the account that gets the mail you want to block, not a different one.

steps.name: Open a message from the sender
steps.text: Click any email from the address you want to block. Read the sender line before you go on. The block applies to that exact address, so a lookalike address needs its own block.
steps.tip: Compare the full address with the name shown. Scammers often reuse a familiar name with a different address.

steps.name: Click More next to Reply
steps.text: Find Reply at the top right of the open message. Click the three dots next to it. Google's help page calls this button More.

steps.name: Choose Block followed by the sender
steps.text: In the menu, click Block followed by the sender's name or address. Google's help page does not describe a confirmation message, so the menu is your only check.
steps.tip: The item should show the sender you expect. If it does not, close the menu and check the sender line again.

steps.name: Check where future mail goes
steps.text: Future mail from that address goes to Spam, not your inbox. Older messages from the sender stay where they are. Check Spam the next time the sender writes.
steps.tip: Do not empty Spam to reset the block. Gmail still flags the sender's mail as spam.

troubleshooting.problem: Mail from the sender still reaches your inbox
troubleshooting.fix: Check Spam first. Then look for a filter that labels or forwards the mail, or a second address the sender used. Blocking works per address, so a new address needs its own block.

troubleshooting.problem: The Block item is missing from the menu
troubleshooting.fix: Open the message itself, then click More next to Reply. If you still see no Block item, use the inbox-list route or the Apple Mail steps in this guide.
Go to Settings > See all settings > Filters and blocked addresses, tick the address, and click Unblock selected addresses.
Turn on Keyboard shortcuts in Settings > See all settings > Settings, then click Save Changes. Shortcuts do nothing until you do.

troubleshooting.problem: Blocked mail still shows in your Apple Mail inbox
troubleshooting.fix: Open Mail > Preferences, or Mail > Settings on macOS 27, then choose Junk Mail > Blocked. Keep Enable blocked mail filtering ticked, and choose Move it to the Trash if you do not want to see it.

troubleshooting.problem: A message from a blocked sender has disappeared
troubleshooting.fix: Check Trash and Spam. Google says messages in those folders are permanently deleted after 30 days, so check soon.
